story.title: Mohamed Salah Joins Trabzonspor on Two-Year Deal
story.summary: Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year contract with Turkish club Trabzonspor after leaving Liverpool, where he spent nine years. During his time at Liverpool, Salah scored 257 goals in 442 appearances and won two Premier League titles and a Champions League trophy. His new contract reportedly includes a salary of 17 million euros per season.

explore_lenses.label: How did Salah reach this departure?
explore_lenses.title: A planned Liverpool exit ended a nine-year era
explore_lenses.summary: Liverpool announced Salah’s departure in March, framing it as an agreed end to his nine-year spell rather than an abrupt transfer. The final weeks were marked by a public farewell and Salah’s own emphasis on his bond with the club and supporters.

claims.text: Liverpool announced on March 24 that Salah had reached an agreement to leave at the end of the 2025-26 season, closing a nine-year chapter that began with his 2017 arrival from Roma.
Liverpool’s final accounting credited Salah with 257 goals and 120 assists in 442 appearances; it said only Ian Rush and Roger Hunt scored more goals for the club.

After Liverpool’s final match, Salah described leaving as difficult and said the players had given their youth to the club; this is Salah’s perspective, not an explanation of the club’s transfer strategy.

story_report.summary: Egyptian forward Mohamed Salah has signed a two-year contract with Trabzonspor after leaving Liverpool at the end of a nine-year spell. His salary at the Turkish club is reported to be 17 million euros per season. The move gives Trabzonspor a prolific former Liverpool forward as the club prepares for the Europa League playoff round after finishing third in the 2025-26 Turkish Super Lig.

sections.heading: Salah’s Liverpool Record
sections.body: Liverpool announced on March 24 that Salah had agreed to leave after the 2025-26 season, ending a chapter that began with his arrival from Roma in 2017. The club’s final tally credited him with 257 goals and 120 assists in 442 appearances, with only Ian Rush and Roger Hunt scoring more Liverpool goals. Salah won two Premier League titles and the Champions League during his time at Anfield.

sections.heading: Trabzonspor’s European Campaign
sections.body: Trabzonspor qualified for the Europa League playoff round by finishing third in the 2025-26 Turkish Super Lig. UEFA’s Champions League club page lists the club as not playing in the 2026-27 Champions League, making the Europa League route its confirmed European competition pathway in the reviewed evidence. Reuters reporting said Salah was due to complete his signing ceremony on August 6 after arriving in Türkiye.

unresolved.text: The reviewed sources do not identify Trabzonspor’s Europa League playoff opponent or match dates, or say whether Salah has been registered to play in those fixtures.
The reviewed Liverpool and transfer reports do not provide the full private reasons or financial terms behind the agreement ending Salah’s Liverpool contract.

related_stories.title: FIFA Leadership Reaffirms Support for Infantino After Crisis Meeting
related_stories.summary: FIFA held a crisis meeting in Morocco where officials expressed their full support for President Gianni Infantino, despite recent controversies surrounding a failed proposal to allow private investment in the World Cup. The organization also issued an apology for the mistakes made during the planning process. Infantino's leadership appears secure for now, as the board aims to move forward from the backlash.

related_stories.title: Israeli Settler Charged in Killing of Palestinian Activist Awdah Hathaleen
related_stories.summary: Israeli prosecutors have charged settler Yinon Levi with the killing of Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen in the occupied West Bank. The indictment, filed in district court, marks the first time an Israeli has been charged for the death of a Palestinian since the October 2023 attacks.

related_stories.title: DR Congo Faces Rapid Resurgence of Ebola Epidemic
related_stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is grappling with a significant resurgence of Ebola, having recorded nearly 4,000 confirmed cases and over 1,800 deaths. This outbreak, attributed to the Bundibugyo virus, is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak in history and the fastest-spreading in the country's records.
